<!--
  FRESH DRAFT of the entanglement figure. Replaces the nested-box design.
  The old files (entanglement-anime.qmd, entanglement-diagram.qmd) are untouched.

  DESIGN CONTRACT
  - Two stacked rows, IDENTICAL output bar at the end of each (one <use> of one
    <defs> group, so they cannot drift apart).
  - The output is always woven. Content+format are never drawn as separate boxes
    and never as a box-inside-a-box (containment is the visual opposite of
    entanglement). They are interleaved stripes.
  - The difference between the rows is NOT what comes out. It is:
      (a) WHEN the weaving happens, and
      (b) therefore whether you can still EDIT the content yourself.
    Row 1: the only lever on the content is review & re-prompt.
    Row 2: you edit the content (or the structure) directly; the agent is a
    one-shot, not a loop.
  - The empty gap in row 1 between agent and output is deliberate: it is exactly
    the space that Quarto fills in row 2.
  - amber = content/data, blue = structure/format, green = the human's direct
    action. A legend states the first two, since the striped bar is the only
    place the audience meets those colors.
  - The agent is PROBABILISTIC and both rows say so: dashed box (the stochastic
    component) plus, in row 1 only, a stack of faded ghost documents with
    different stripes — the runs you didn't get. Row 2 has no ghosts because
    render is deterministic; that contrast is the point. The ghosts are their
    own defs groups, never #doc, so the two real outputs stay identical.

  BUILD: base + 2 fragments = 3 states, 2 clicks.
    state 1  row 1 (the status quo): one pass, re-prompt is your only lever
    state 2  row 2 appears: agent writes only the .qmd, data is separate, render
    state 3  green edit arrows + the payoff line

  Pure SVG + reveal fragments. No anime.js, no CDN, nothing to vendor before
  the talk. Fragments toggle group opacity, which is all this needs.

  ONE SLIDE ONLY. No title slide (no title/subtitle in the YAML) and no visible
  heading — the `##` is an empty ATX heading that exists solely to open the
  slide, hidden by the h2:empty rule below.
-->

::: {.notes}
Both of these weave content and format together. The only question is when — and
by what.

Click 1: the status quo. Amber is my content, blue is the structure — and by the
time I see the document they're fused. One probabilistic pass wove them together.
Note the dashed box, and the faded copies behind the document: that step is a
draw, not a computation. Same prompt tomorrow, different document. So if a
sentence is wrong, I can't go in and change it. All I can do is review and ask
again, and get a whole new document back.

Click 2: same prompt, same agent — but now it writes the `.qmd`. The data sits
beside it. Render puts them together. The agent is still probabilistic — it's
still dashed — but now only the *structure* it writes can vary. Render itself is
deterministic, so there are no ghosts back here. And the output is *identical*.
I have not made a better document.

Click 3: what I've actually bought. The content is still mine to touch — I edit
the data, or the `.qmd`, directly. The agent ran once; I'm not looping through it
to get at my own sentences.

Optional, for this room: "weave" isn't my metaphor. It's literate programming's
own word — Sweave, then knitr. Quarto has always been a weaving tool. I'm just
arguing we should weave later.
:::
